_comment: Canonical Team Atlas scenario — single source of truth for all Phase 3 documentation surfaces. Do not copy values into individual pages; reference this file or derive from it.
canonical_opening_request:
Show me the whole Atlas team backlog across APP and API.

Include the current sprint, open backlog, unassigned work, and blocked issues.

Group everything into:

- ready to pull
- needs story work
- blocked
- in progress

Recommend five items for the team to discuss next.

Do not change Jira.
scope_clarification_prompt:
I found two possible Atlas scopes:

1. The Atlas Jira board
2. Issues whose Team field is Atlas

Which should I use?
coverage_disclosure: Complete — 184 items (APP: 127, API: 57 · Sprint 23 + open backlog · as of today)
jira_unchanged_statement: Jira was not changed by this run.

APP-206.title: User cannot reset password when SSO is enabled
APP-206.readiness_gap: Missing: expected behaviour when SSO provider is unavailable; no acceptance criteria covering the SSO-unavailable path
APP-206.gap_detail: Fails Q2 (acceptance criteria) — the description covers the happy path but does not specify what happens when the identity provider returns an error or times out. Engineering cannot begin without knowing whether to show a fallback or block the reset.
APP-206.proposed_description:
When a user attempts to reset their password and their account is SSO-enabled:

- If the SSO provider is reachable: redirect to the SSO provider's reset flow.
- If the SSO provider is unreachable or returns an error: display 'Your account uses single sign-on. Contact your IT administrator to reset your password.' Do not allow direct password reset as a fallback.
- Log the provider error for the ops team.
proposed_acs: Given SSO-enabled user requests password reset, when SSO provider is reachable, then user is redirected to SSO provider reset flow
Given SSO-enabled user requests password reset, when SSO provider is unreachable, then user sees the contact-IT message and cannot set a password directly
Given SSO provider returns an error, then the error is logged with provider name and HTTP status
APP-206.unresolved_question: Should the system allow a temporary bypass for locked-out SSO admins? Needs product owner decision.
APP-206.expected_readiness_after_draft: APP-206 would pass Q1, Q2, and Q3 — it would reach Ready to pull once the product owner answers the bypass question.

APP-219.title: Export to CSV drops custom field values
APP-219.readiness_gap: No acceptance criteria; no reproduction steps; scope of 'custom fields' is undefined
APP-219.gap_detail: Fails Q1 (clear outcome) and Q2 (acceptance criteria) — it is unclear which custom field types are affected (text, select, multi-select, date?), which export path (UI button vs API) is broken, and what 'drops' means (empty string, omitted column, null?).
APP-219.proposed_description:
When a user exports issues to CSV from the issue list view:

- All configured custom field columns must appear in the CSV header row.
- Each row must include the field value for that issue, or an empty string if the field has no value for that issue.
- Custom field types in scope: text, single select, multi-select (pipe-delimited), date (ISO 8601).
- Out of scope for this ticket: API export endpoint and attachment fields.
proposed_acs: Given an issue list with custom fields configured, when the user clicks Export to CSV, then the CSV header row includes all custom field names
Given an issue with a single-select custom field set, when exported to CSV, then the value appears in the correct column
Given an issue with a multi-select custom field set to two values, when exported to CSV, then both values appear pipe-delimited in the correct column
Given an issue with no value for a custom field, when exported to CSV, then an empty string appears in that column (not a missing column)
APP-219.unresolved_question: Which custom field types are in scope — are lookup/user-picker fields included or deferred?
APP-219.expected_readiness_after_draft: APP-219 would pass Q1 and Q2 after the product owner confirms field-type scope. It would reach Needs story work → Ready to pull in one revision.
APP-219.write_failure_reason: 403 Forbidden — your token does not have edit permission on APP-219 (reporter-only access). The proposed rewrite was NOT applied.
APP-219.recovery_action: Retry APP-219 manually via `jira: update-issue APP-219` with the description and acceptance criteria above once you have edit access, or ask the issue owner to apply the draft.

API-104.title: Rate-limit response should include Retry-After header
API-104.readiness_gap: Acceptance criteria are present but the retry interval is unspecified; no error response schema documented
API-104.gap_detail: Fails Q2 partially — ACs mention the header but do not specify the format (seconds vs HTTP date), the value source (fixed vs dynamic), or what clients should do when the header is absent.
API-104.proposed_description:
When the API gateway returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests:

- The response MUST include a `Retry-After` header.
- The value MUST be an integer number of seconds (e.g. `Retry-After: 60`).
- The value MUST be sourced from the rate-limiter's token-bucket drain time, rounded up to the nearest second.
- If the drain time is unavailable, use a fixed fallback of 30 seconds.
- The response body MUST include `{"error": "rate_limited", "retry_after_seconds": <value>}`.
proposed_acs: Given a client exceeds the rate limit, when the API returns 429, then the response includes Retry-After: <integer seconds>
Given the token-bucket drain time is known, when 429 is returned, then Retry-After value equals ceil(drain_seconds)
Given drain time is unavailable, when 429 is returned, then Retry-After value is 30
Given any 429 response, then body contains {"error": "rate_limited", "retry_after_seconds": <integer>}
API-104.expected_readiness_after_draft: API-104 would pass all five questions — it would reach Ready to pull immediately after the draft is accepted.

terminology.whole_team_backlog: All open work for the selected team scope across the configured projects, sprint, and backlog.
terminology.ready_to_pull: Work that is in scope, in an eligible open-work state, has no known unresolved blocker, and has enough definition for the team to begin under the configured readiness criteria.
terminology.needs_story_work: Work that is open but lacks enough definition to begin — missing acceptance criteria, unclear scope, or an unresolved question that blocks engineering.
terminology.blocked: Work with a known unresolved dependency, external decision, or blocker that prevents the team from starting or continuing.
terminology.in_progress: Work currently being actively worked on by a team member.
terminology.other_open_work: Open work that does not fit the above categories — not ready, not blocked, not in progress, not assignable today.
terminology.needs_confirmation: When readiness cannot be established — the status is unclear or the scope is ambiguous.
terminology.draft_improvement: A proposed rewrite of a story's description or acceptance criteria, produced by jira-story-triage, that has not been written to Jira.
terminology.proposed_jira_update: A Jira write that has been shown to the user (exact fields, old and new values) but not yet confirmed.
terminology.approved_jira_update: A proposed Jira update that the user has explicitly confirmed; the write then occurs.
terminology.team_summary: A read-only stand-up or status summary generated from the backlog data.
terminology.confluence_ready_draft: A formatted draft of the team summary, prepared for Confluence but not yet published.
terminology.agent_ready: An optional lens, only applied when explicitly requested: work that meets a five-question readiness bar suitable for autonomous coding-agent execution. Not the same as ready to pull.
